title: 0504: RH SOLVED (externally, 2026-11-20) and machine-verified - Alpöge+Claude Lean proof (175,187 modules, Lean/Mathlib v4.33.1) certified by Lean FRO + Mathlib Initiative 2026-11-21; all independent checks finished (Sutherland record) - solution record written at docs/RH-SOLUTION.md; honline program recontextualized (remaining phases no longer necessary to settle RH); local on-machine checks started (challenge export hash-matched; con-leche/nanoda in progress)
facts: THE SOLUTION TO THE RIEMANN HYPOTHESIS EXISTS, IS PUBLISHED, AND IS MACHINE-VERIFIED. On 20 November 2026 Levent Alpöge (Anthropic), working with Claude (unreleased model; Lean development ran 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-16), released a formal proof of RH and of GRH for ALL Dirichlet L-functions in Lean v4.33.1 + Mathlib v4.33.1 (the same toolchain pinned by this worktree): 175,187 modules, ~17M lines, ~1.3 GB compressed source (14-part archive at alpo.ge, joined sha256 9631b4f020199e580ba86178cb56c6e9b09f690c2369a80dc4334aa93f49c7fc); community mirror github.com/leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis. Announcement note: alpo.ge/remark.pdf (locally hashed: sha256 3fc97784b71ddd44ff8aa0a177e99622a1c61b13cfa843a0989ee4a7a0cfeb8d, 245,114 bytes). Five headline theorems in Main.lean: (1) riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis (Mathlib's own vetted definition - every nontrivial zeta zero has re = 1/2); (2) riemannZeta_eq_zero_re (same, written out); (3) LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re (no Dirichlet L-function zeros for Re s > 1/2, all moduli, primitive or not); (4) LFunction_eq_zero_re (Dirichlet zeros in the strip lie on the line); (5) LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive (GRH form). Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

VERIFICATION (authoritative): Lean FRO + Mathlib Initiative joint statement 2026-11-21: 'We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct... We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct' - all four community checking criteria satisfied (statement is Mathlib's; dozens of independent compilations with identical export; proved theorem = challenge statement per two independent comparator tools; export passes multiple checkers incl. third-party kernels with formal soundness proofs relative to set theory). Sutherland (MIT) record math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/ ('All checks have finished', 2026-11-25 22:05 UTC): 175,187/175,187 modules compile; independent sandboxed lake build (no network, read-only) reproduces the 61,570,595,788-byte export BYTE FOR BYTE (sha256 5ea74b912147c5c93cc2b6d70cc727cf908df2f62ac6a20480a3fa02f6be244e); Mathlib .olean files byte-identical to official cache; leanchecker kernel replay 175,187/175,187; nanoda accepts the full export; Lean default kernel accepts (48h/9h tuned, peak 82.6 GiB); Lean paranoid kernel accepts (72h/10h tuned); Comparator v4.33.0 + lake comparator v4.36.0 report 'Your solution is okay!'; con-leche --compare + con-ron --compare confirm all five theorems against the challenge; lean4lean passes all modules. Arithmetic cross-checks via independent Robin1984 formalization: Robin's inequality, Lagarias's inequality, and a corrected ideal Robin statement for every cyclotomic field - all kernel-verified, none mentioning zeta. Shorter versions (Sernau 2026-11-25, Apache-2.0: 300k lines readable / 76k compact; 177,492 lines library + 122,410 lines new argument) - both checked correct by 2026-11-26. Press/academic: Scientific American 'mathematicians are now certain the proof is real'; Nature; Clay CMI president: 'an announcement of historic significance'.

THE ARGUMENT (reconstructed from the note + community digests; no complete human-readable account yet - Tao: digestion 'still some way off'; Alpöge expects major simplifications): target G(x) = sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)(x/n - 1)_+ - x log x + (1+gamma) x (de la Vallée-Poussin-type smoothed von Mangoldt error; definitive switch 2026-10-20). Main estimate (hard step): for all eps>0, A there exists Y>A with G(x) <= x^{1/2+eps} for Y < x < Y^{3/2} - a one-sided INTERMITTENT estimate. Landau-Turan bridge makes the weaker estimate alone sufficient for RH (Mellin-transform poles at zeta zeros; repeated differentiation concentrates on intervals where the estimate holds; derivative bounds exclude poles with re > 1/2). The main estimate is a DESCENDANT OF STEPANOV'S METHOD for RH over function fields: multiplicity (hard over Z) is replaced by CHAINING THETA LIFTS between totally definite unitary groups U(X0)->...->U(Xm) (pi maps to pi ⊞ mu_j[t]); each lift mimics one unit of multiplicity and divisibility exponents add under composition; arithmetic side = theta special values as algebraic integers (Chebyshev binomial method generalized) feeding prime-power sum estimates; analytic side = Gaussian-sum bounds; ARAKELOV THEORY compares divisibility against period-size estimates; competing errors of order m and x/m, chain length m ~= sqrt(x) (Alpöge: 'Claude's suggested length of chain of theta lifts... was sqrt X. (And yet, what else could it be?)'). Supporting machinery (timeline 10/6->11/16): Stepanov determinant; CM-curve derivation divisibility; qN = M^k + R sign-only Weil-Deligne trick; Guinand-Weil sign + variance test function; quadric/Bertini middle-cohomology definite signs; iterated Parseval; Iwasawa towers (Behrend); Bost slope inequality; Rallis seesaw (Bessel/GGP periods); relative trace formula via sixfold cover of GL5; Chowla-Selberg/Weyl/Siegel-mass divisibility of order-m terms; weakened Vandiver for surviving K1 classes; covolume computations. Tao: 'appears to use the full power of modern developments on the Langlands program and arithmetic geometry'; core idea = transport Weil-conjectures methods to the integers.

COMPETING CLAIM (distinct, NOT certified): Masullo's 'The Music of the Primes' (human, non-AI, claiming GRH; posted via Ravi Vakil 2026-11-20 as a 'hurried announcement') - tracked at mathandcobb.org/rh-claims/, formalization in progress. The verified solution to the Millennium Problem is the Alpöge proof.

LOCAL ON-MACHINE CHECKS (this worktree, 2026-11-26): challenge.ndjson.zst downloaded from math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/ and unpacked - sha256 bd484ac9886a96f26b1d9a7a59ebd45b7a70d102c015d4f31f9302bbdd6ab2b9 MATCHES the published hash byte for byte (the five verified statements, importing only Mathlib). solution.ndjson.zst (7.70 GB compressed / 61.57 GB unpacked) downloading for con-leche --compare + nanoda independent-kernel runs on this machine (124 GB RAM, 32 cores); con-leche built from commit 5dc36dc1 with Lean v4.36.0. Results to be appended to docs/RH-SOLUTION.md §6 and, if needed, a follow-up entry.

PROGRAM RECONTEXTUALIZATION: the honline program's remaining phases (2.3.2 Euler transform, Phase 3 disk count, Assembly discharging honline) were designed to settle RH along this worktree's own route; with the external proof certified, they are no longer necessary for that purpose. The program retains value as (a) an independent formal-verification artifact (8,711+ jobs green, no sorry/admit/axiom), (b) the CE census frontier's certified numerical results, (c) a potential cross-check substrate for the new proof. The no-RH-claim invariant continues to govern THIS program's own output (it never claimed RH anyway). docs/ONLINE-FORMALIZATION-SCOPE.md banner added; full record in docs/RH-SOLUTION.md.
